nodes.label: Auto-Clarity Exception
nodes.rationale: Drop caveman mode temporarily for security warnings, irreversible-action confirmations, and multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread; resume after the clear part.

nodes.label: Design It Twice
nodes.rationale: Your first idea is unlikely to be the best; generate multiple radically different designs, then compare.

nodes.label: Diagnostic Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: A fast, deterministic, agent-runnable pass/fail signal is the skill itself - bisection, hypothesis-testing, and instrumentation all just consume it; build the loop first, refuse to proceed to hypotheses without it.

nodes.label: HITL Loop Template Script
nodes.rationale: Last resort: when a human must click, drive them with scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh so the feedback loop stays structured and output feeds back to the agent.

nodes.label: Information as a Directed Acyclic Graph
nodes.rationale: Information is a directed acyclic graph - section order and contents must respect information dependencies.

nodes.label: PreToolUse Hook Pattern
nodes.rationale: A PreToolUse command hook intercepts dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, checkout/restore .) before Claude executes them.

nodes.label: ADR Offering Criteria
nodes.rationale: Offer an ADR only when the decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off - the value is recording that a decision was made and why, not filling in sections.

nodes.label: Seam
nodes.rationale: Seam (from Michael Feathers): a place where you can alter behaviour without editing in that place; 'boundary' is rejected as overloaded with DDD's bounded context.

nodes.label: Depth
nodes.rationale: Depth-as-leverage rather than Ousterhout's ratio of implementation lines to interface lines - the ratio rewards padding the implementation.

nodes.label: Adapter
nodes.rationale: A concrete thing that satisfies an interface at a seam; one adapter means a hypothetical seam, two adapters mean a real one.

nodes.label: @total-typescript/shoehorn
nodes.rationale: Pass partial data in tests while keeping TypeScript happy; replaces with type-safe alternatives: fromPartial() for partial data, fromAny() for intentionally wrong data, fromExact() to force full objects. Test code only.

nodes.label: Index Notes Pattern
nodes.rationale: No folders for organization - use [[wikilinks]] and index notes (lists of wikilinks) instead.

nodes.label: Logic Prototype
nodes.rationale: Tiny interactive terminal app to drive a state model by hand for business-logic/state-transition/data-shape questions; isolate logic in a pure portable module; the TUI shell is throwaway.

nodes.label: Prototype
nodes.rationale: A prototype is throwaway code that answers a question; the question decides the shape; the answer is the only thing worth keeping.

nodes.label: UI Prototype
nodes.rationale: Several radically different UI variations on a single route, switchable via ?variant= and a floating bottom bar; variants must differ structurally, not just in colour.

nodes.label: Request Refactor Plan
nodes.rationale: Detailed refactor plan with tiny commits produced via user interview, then filed as a GitHub issue.

nodes.label: Refactor Requirements Interview
nodes.rationale: Explore the repo first to verify the user's assertions; interview must be extremely detailed; hammer out exact scope of change.

nodes.label: Tiny Commits Plan
nodes.rationale: Martin Fowler: make each refactoring step as small as possible so you can always see the program working; each commit leaves the codebase working.

nodes.label: Refactor Plan Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Sections: Problem, Solution, Commits, Decision Document, Testing Decisions, Out of Scope. No file paths or code snippets - they go stale quickly.

nodes.label: Testing Decisions Guidance
nodes.rationale: Good tests only test external behavior, not implementation details; record tested modules and prior art.

nodes.label: Two-Axis Review Skill
nodes.rationale: Reviews diff between HEAD and a fixed point via three-dot merge-base diff, along two independent axes.

nodes.label: Standards Review Axis
nodes.rationale: Conformance to repo-documented coding standards; note machine-enforced ones but do not re-check what tooling checks.

nodes.label: Spec Review Axis
nodes.rationale: Flags missing/partial requirements, scope creep, and wrong-looking implementations, quoting the spec line per finding.

nodes.label: Parallel Sub-Agent Review Execution
nodes.rationale: Two sub-agents run in parallel so their contexts don't pollute each other; findings reported verbatim, not merged.

nodes.label: Why Two Axes
nodes.rationale: A change can pass one axis and fail the other; separate reporting stops one axis masking the other.

nodes.label: Scaffold Exercises Skill
nodes.rationale: Create exercise directory structures that pass pnpm ai-hero-cli internal lint, then commit.

nodes.label: Exercise Directory Naming Scheme
nodes.rationale: Sections XX-section-name, exercises XX.YY-exercise-name inside sections; dash-case lowercase names.

nodes.label: Exercise Variants (problem-solution-explain)
nodes.rationale: Each exercise needs problem/, solution/ and/or explainer/ subfolders; default to explainer/ when stubbing.

nodes.label: Scaffold Lint Gate (ai-hero-cli)
nodes.rationale: Linter checks variant subfolders, non-empty readme.md, no .gitkeep/speaker-notes/broken links, main.ts when code present.

nodes.label: git mv Rename Workflow
nodes.rationale: Use git mv, not mv, when renumbering exercises to preserve git history.

nodes.label: Setup Matt Pocock's Skills
nodes.rationale: Per-repo config for engineering skills: issue tracker, triage labels, domain docs; prompt-driven, not deterministic.

nodes.label: Agent Skills Block
nodes.rationale: ## Agent skills block added to CLAUDE.md if present else AGENTS.md; update in place, never create both.

nodes.label: Issue Tracker Decision (Section A)
nodes.rationale: Skills read/write issues; they need to know whether to call gh, glab, write .scratch/ markdown, or another workflow.

nodes.label: Triage Label Decision (Section B)
nodes.rationale: Five canonical roles mapped to the repo's actual label strings so the triage skill applies the right labels instead of creating duplicates.

nodes.label: Domain Docs Decision (Section C)
nodes.rationale: Single-context vs multi-context (CONTEXT-MAP.md) so skills look in the right place.

nodes.label: Domain Docs Consumer Rules
nodes.rationale: Read CONTEXT.md/CONTEXT-MAP.md plus docs/adr before exploring; if absent proceed silently (producer creates lazily).

nodes.label: Multi-Context Repository Layout
nodes.rationale: CONTEXT-MAP.md at root points to per-context CONTEXT.md files (monorepo); context-scoped ADRs under src/<context>/docs/adr/.

nodes.label: Glossary Vocabulary Adherence
nodes.rationale: Use terms as defined in CONTEXT.md; missing glossary term signals invented language or a real gap for /grill-with-docs.

nodes.label: ADR Conflict Flagging
nodes.rationale: Surface ADR contradictions explicitly rather than silently overriding.

nodes.label: grill-with-docs Producer Skill
nodes.rationale: Creates CONTEXT.md glossary and ADRs lazily when terms or decisions get resolved.

nodes.label: GitHub Issue Tracker Doc
nodes.rationale: Issues and PRDs live as GitHub issues; all operations via gh CLI.

nodes.label: gh CLI Conventions
nodes.rationale: gh issue create/view/list/comment/edit/close; repo inferred from git remote -v.

nodes.label: Publish/Fetch Mapping (GitHub)
nodes.rationale: 'Publish to the issue tracker' means create a GitHub issue; 'fetch the relevant ticket' runs gh issue view --comments.

nodes.label: GitLab Issue Tracker Doc
nodes.rationale: Issues and PRDs live as GitLab issues; all operations via glab CLI.

nodes.label: glab CLI Conventions
nodes.rationale: glab issue create/view/list/note/update/close; repo inferred from git remote -v.

nodes.label: Merge Request Terminology
nodes.rationale: GitLab calls PRs merge requests and comments notes; close takes no comment so post the note first.

nodes.label: Local Markdown Issue Tracker Doc
nodes.rationale: Issues and PRDs live as markdown files under .scratch/ - for solo projects or repos without a remote.

nodes.label: .scratch/ Feature-Slug Layout
nodes.rationale: One directory per feature .scratch/<feature-slug>/; PRD.md at root, implementation issues numbered from 01 under issues/.

nodes.label: Local Status Line Triage
nodes.rationale: Triage state recorded as a Status: line near the top; comments append under a ## Comments heading.

nodes.label: Triage Labels Mapping Doc
nodes.rationale: Table mapping five canonical roles to the repo's actual label strings; skills apply labels by role.

nodes.label: Five Canonical Triage Roles
nodes.rationale: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix - the triage state machine.

nodes.label: ready-for-agent Role (AFK-Ready)
nodes.rationale: Fully specified, AFK-ready: an agent can pick it up with no human context.

nodes.label: mattpocock/skills Label Source
nodes.rationale: Canonical role strings originate from the mattpocock/skills reference repo.

nodes.label: Setup Pre-Commit Hooks
nodes.rationale: Install Husky + lint-staged + Prettier and wire typecheck/test into pre-commit.

nodes.label: Husky Pre-Commit Hook
nodes.rationale: .husky/pre-commit runs lint-staged then typecheck then tests; no shebang needed for Husky v9+.

nodes.label: lint-staged + Prettier
nodes.rationale: Prettier on staged files only (fast); --ignore-unknown skips unparseable files; .prettierrc created only if missing.

nodes.label: Typecheck and Test Gate
nodes.rationale: Full typecheck and tests run after lint-staged; omitted if repo lacks such scripts.

nodes.label: Package Manager Detection
nodes.rationale: npm/pnpm/yarn/bun detected from lockfiles; default npm if unclear.

nodes.label: Test-Driven Development Skill
nodes.rationale: Red-green-refactor with vertical tracer-bullet slices; tests verify behavior through public interfaces only.

nodes.label: Behavior-Over-Implementation Principle
nodes.rationale: Core principle: code can change entirely, tests shouldn't; tests describe WHAT not HOW; they survive refactors.

nodes.label: Red-Green-Refactor Loop
nodes.rationale: One test at a time; only enough code to pass; never refactor while RED.

nodes.label: Tracer Bullet Vertical Slices
nodes.rationale: One test then one implementation, repeated; each test responds to what the previous cycle learned.

nodes.label: Horizontal Slices Anti-Pattern
nodes.rationale: All tests first then all implementation produces crap tests of imagined behavior; tests become insensitive to real changes.

nodes.label: TDD Planning Phase
nodes.rationale: Use domain glossary and ADRs; confirm interfaces and behaviors to test; focus on critical paths, not every edge case.

nodes.label: Deep Modules
nodes.rationale: Small interface + lots of implementation; hide complex logic behind few methods and simple params.

nodes.label: Shallow Modules
nodes.rationale: Large interface + thin implementation that just passes through - to be avoided.

nodes.label: A Philosophy of Software Design (source)
nodes.rationale: Cited source for the deep-module concept.

nodes.label: Interface Reduction Questions
nodes.rationale: Fewer methods, simpler params, hide more complexity - the design questions when shaping interfaces.

nodes.label: Interface Design for Testability
nodes.rationale: Good interfaces make testing natural: accept dependencies, return results, small surface area.

nodes.label: Accept Dependencies, Do Not Create Them
nodes.rationale: Testable: processOrder(order, paymentGateway); hard to test: constructor news up the gateway.

nodes.label: Return Results, Avoid Side Effects
nodes.rationale: calculateDiscount(cart): Discount is testable; applyDiscount mutating a cart is not.

nodes.label: Small Surface Area Rule
nodes.rationale: Fewer methods and params mean fewer tests and simpler setup.

nodes.label: When to Mock
nodes.rationale: Mock only at system boundaries; never your own modules, internal collaborators, or anything you control.

nodes.label: Mock at System Boundaries Only
nodes.rationale: External APIs, occasionally databases, time/randomness, file system.

nodes.label: Designing for Mockability
nodes.rationale: Dependency injection at boundaries plus SDK-style interfaces.

nodes.label: SDK-Style Interfaces Over Generic Fetchers
nodes.rationale: Specific functions per endpoint mock cleanly; generic fetch requires conditional logic inside mocks.

nodes.label: Refactor Candidates
nodes.rationale: Run tests after each refactor step; never refactor while RED.

nodes.label: Smell to Refactor Catalogue
nodes.rationale: Duplication, long methods, shallow modules, feature envy, primitive obsession; keep tests on the public interface.

nodes.label: Good and Bad Tests
nodes.rationale: Tests behavior users care about through the public API; survives internal refactors.

nodes.label: Good Test Characteristics
nodes.rationale: Integration-style, describes WHAT not HOW, one logical assertion per test.

nodes.label: Bad Test Red Flags
nodes.rationale: Mocking internal collaborators, testing private methods, asserting call counts, name describes HOW, verifying via DB query instead of interface.

nodes.label: GLOSSARY.md Format
nodes.rationale: Canonical language of the workspace; all explainers, exercises and learning records adhere to its terminology.

nodes.label: Glossary Building as Learning Evidence
nodes.rationale: Compressing a concept into a tight definition is evidence the user understands it.

nodes.label: Glossary Writing Rules
nodes.rationale: Opinionated (one best term, aliases to avoid), tight 1-2 sentence definitions, use glossary terms inside definitions, flag ambiguities, revise.

nodes.label: Learning Record Format
nodes.rationale: Teaching equivalent of ADRs - non-obvious lessons and key insights that steer future sessions; not a journal.

nodes.label: When to Write a Learning Record
nodes.rationale: Genuine understanding, disclosed prior knowledge, corrected misconceptions, or mission shifts; coverage alone does not qualify.

nodes.label: Learning Record Supersession
nodes.rationale: Mark old records superseded by LR-NNNN rather than deleting; evolution history is useful signal.

nodes.label: MISSION.md Format
nodes.rationale: Captures why the user learns the topic; every teaching decision traces back to it.

nodes.label: Concrete Mission Goals
nodes.rationale: Observable outcomes over abstract framings; a bad mission is worse than no mission.

nodes.label: Mission Constraints and Out of Scope
nodes.rationale: Adjacent topics explicitly excluded protect the zone of proximal development.

nodes.label: RESOURCES.md Format
nodes.rationale: Curated set of trusted sources; knowledge drawn from here, never parametric guesses.

nodes.label: Knowledge/Wisdom Resource Grouping
nodes.rationale: Groups by Knowledge and Wisdom (Communities), mirroring the philosophy in SKILL.md.

nodes.label: Resource Curation Rules
nodes.rationale: High-trust only, annotate every entry, surface gaps as ## Gaps, prune ruthlessly, record community preferences.

nodes.label: teach Skill
nodes.rationale: Stateful multi-session teaching skill grounded in a workspace of mission, resources and learning records.

nodes.label: Teaching Workspace Structure
nodes.rationale: MISSION.md, reference/*.html, RESOURCES.md, learning-records/, lessons/, NOTES.md capture cross-session state.

nodes.label: Knowledge Skills Wisdom Philosophy
nodes.rationale: Knowledge from high-trust resources, skills via interactive lessons, wisdom from communities; never trust parametric knowledge.

nodes.label: Fluency vs Storage Strength
nodes.rationale: Fluency is illusory mastery; storage strength is the real goal built via retrieval practice, spacing, interleaving.

nodes.label: Zone of Proximal Development
nodes.rationale: Challenge the user 'just enough' each lesson; computed from learning-records and the mission.

nodes.label: Lesson Unit
nodes.rationale: Single self-contained HTML file per tightly-scoped thing; beautiful, short, mission-tied, links via anchors, recommends a primary source.

nodes.label: Reference Documents
nodes.rationale: Compressed essence of lessons for quick reference (cheat sheets, algorithms, glossaries) - reviewed long after lessons.

nodes.label: Feedback Loops
nodes.rationale: Tightest possible immediate (ideally automatic) feedback; quiz answers equal-length to avoid hinting.

nodes.label: Communities for Wisdom
nodes.rationale: Wisdom questions delegate to high-reputation communities where the user can test skills; respect opt-out preference.

nodes.label: Data Honesty: Missing Is Never Zero (R9)
nodes.rationale: Fourteen panel states distinguish missing/empty/unavailable; RESOURCE_NOT_PROVIDED, an empty result and a value of zero are three different facts and must never render alike.

nodes.label: Free-Tier Intraday Binding Constraint
nodes.rationale: Every paid provider (ICE, LSEG, TickData, NSE authorised vendors) is out; free intraday is shallow (days-to-months windows), free tick and depth effectively do not exist for NSE, so depth is out of scope permanently.

nodes.label: Measure Modelling Quality Before Buying Data
nodes.rationale: Every gauntlet verdict must carry the conditions it was earned under (resolution, historyDays, regimesCovered, costModel, depth); more trades from less history is not more evidence and is exactly what the deflated Sharpe exists to punish.

nodes.label: Two-Repo Hard Boundary (FOREIGN_TREE)
nodes.rationale: E:/BoraTradingTool (TypeScript, Claude Code) and E:/Trading_BOT (Python, OpenCode) are two trees with two owners; TREE_OWNERSHIP makes authorizeWrite return FOREIGN_TREE, and agents coordinate only through runtime/bridge/{claims,requests,responses}.

nodes.label: PriceDomain Gap (Critical)
nodes.rationale: lib/backtest/engine.ts computes (exit-entry)/entry, a ratio; the day a CONTINUOUS_ADDITIVE series reaches it every return is silently wrong; additive levels are never comparable across instruments, roll methodologies or dataset versions.

nodes.label: Reuse Not Rebuild: Feed the Existing Gauntlet
nodes.rationale: Prompt 4 must not build a validation lab; holdout firewall, trial ledger, deflated Sharpe, PBO/CSCV, ablation and promotion ladder already exist and are test-enforced in TypeScript; only unmapped items (ablation variants, matched controls, outlier dependence, window mining, regime partition, latency stress) are implemented.

nodes.label: In-Repo Python Quant Core (quant/)
nodes.rationale: E:/Trading_BOT does not exist on this machine, so v2 routing was wrong; the Python producer lives in a quant/ subtree of this repo joined by the frozen Contract v1 seam - a producer for a seam that was built and left empty.

nodes.label: 1.7% Configuration Survival Funnel Prior
nodes.rationale: Video 1's funnel: 6,190 of 25,000 configs made money after costs and only 420 (1.7%) survived trial correction, cross-instrument cold run and locked holdout; the 15-min bias filter measured 0.16 and the most-cited time-of-day window was not special.

nodes.label: Silent-Corruption-First Build Order
nodes.rationale: Ordered by what would silently corrupt results if left undone: PriceDomain/PriceFrame, point-in-time contract master, causal loader with as_of, sweep detector then ablation, three effective-dated cost schedules, NSE calendar with pre-open states, Kronos PIT archive.

nodes.label: Single-Fault Root Cause (node.exe PATH)
nodes.rationale: All four catalogued start failures were one gap: node.exe lived on Git Bash's PATH but not the Windows PATH, so every lifecycle script via cmd.exe failed and better-sqlite3 never compiled; 'npm rebuild succeeded while doing nothing' and Glob/Read filtering gitignored paths shaped the wrong turns.

nodes.label: Derived, Never Stored Promotion Ladder
nodes.rationale: The ladder (draft -> rehearsed -> validated -> holdout_cleared -> paper_forward -> owner_review) had every stage built and nothing connecting them; Stage is derived from evidence, never stored - a stored stage column would be a second fact about the same thing that can disagree.

nodes.label: Unbiased Forward Validation (forward_outcomes)
nodes.rationale: The prediction is written before the outcome exists; risk denominator fixed at open, resolved observations immutable, win rate withheld below 20 resolved observations because one win is a percentage read as a finding.

nodes.label: Negative Tests (Break It on Purpose)
nodes.rationale: Bad input must be refused, not absorbed; missing resources must render OFFLINE/UNAVAILABLE, never green or zero; missing is never rendered as zero is the system's central claim and the negative tests prove it.

nodes.label: Determinism Spot-Check
nodes.rationale: Any result that moves between runs cannot be used as evidence because the next run is a new trial; the suite includes a test that the seed genuinely changes the outcome.

nodes.label: Autonomy Strip with Cycle Age
nodes.rationale: The autonomy strip is always visible and always specific - mode, age of the last cycle, what it did - fixing the complaint that a badge saying only LEARNING means nothing happened.

nodes.label: Decision-Support Software / Manual Execution Boundary
nodes.rationale: MarketPulse is decision-support software; Paper Research Mode is the only in-application order lifecycle; live-order, approval, heartbeat, portfolio-push and fill-report routes fail closed with EXECUTION_ADAPTER_MISSING and the owner executes manually outside the software.

nodes.label: Kronos: Hypothesis Source, Never a Signal
nodes.rationale: Kronos is admitted as a hypothesis and feature source, never as a signal; forecasts are stamped not_forward_validated by the reader, must beat naive persistence via paired bootstrap, and nothing skips the gauntlet - a pretrained model is a reason to look, never a reason to skip the checks.

nodes.label: NSE + US Equities on Daily Bars (MNQ Out)
nodes.rationale: The candle-only engine decides on close and fills at next open, modelling no spread, queue, partial fill or latency; an MNQ intraday result would be rigorous statistics over a mismeasured input - worse than no backtest; breadth across forty instruments is what makes the multiple-testing correction correct.

nodes.label: Bounded Evidence Package + SHA-256 Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Model input is assembled by the application from a size-bounded evidence snapshot (candles, news, signals, earnings caps) with stable evidence IDs and a SHA-256 hash; the model cannot browse independently and every citation must map to evidence the app can show.
